validation: python3 tools/render_skill.py .claude/skills/<name> && python3 tools/validate_skills.py --only <name> for cap-isolation, cap-agent-runtime, cap-tool-access and cap-telemetry: 0 errors, 0 warnings for all four, checked both before this ceremony's edits (via git stash) and after. No sourced row, quote, definition_of_done, adapters, composes_with or description was touched; every deletion removed a whole proposed row (its origin, text, sources and, where present, quote) rather than editing content within a kept row, confirmed by git diff showing only whole-object removals.
result: cap-isolation 30.65%->28.33% (2 deleted), cap-agent-runtime 31.67%->29.31% (2 deleted), cap-tool-access 32.2%->28.57% (3 deleted), cap-telemetry 31.82%->29.25% (4 deleted). Part total 31.62%->28.93%. All four skills at or under the 30 percent goal (T-t9-02), measured over the whole file (body plus folded). Lever 1 (delete padding) alone closed the gap for all four: 11 rows total, every one a same-skill (or, for cap-telemetry, cross-folded-skill-within-one-file) reword of a sibling row -- either a shape's own field description, an adjacent invariant, an operation's own output text, or a sourced sibling row stating the identical rule. No lever-2 conversion was attempted: every remaining proposed row's quote candidates were already cited by a sibling under the same source id in the same skill, which the brief's restatement-warning rule rules out. Every other proposed row in all four skills, including every folded skill, was left as genuinely-ours per lever 3, most already carrying their own Research query.
